text:
Colorado arrives in good shape, Chicago in a tougher spot. The Avalanche beat Calgary 5-2 on Friday and are 3-2-0 in their last five, though they're without Josh Manson and Zachary L'Heureux. The Blackhawks blew a two-goal lead in Boston, losing 5-4 in overtime, and are 1-3-1 in their last five. COL sits third in the Central, CHI eighth, eight points back. Our numbers have the Blackhawks better than their record: they've created 43% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) but finishing and goaltending have cost them. Bowen Byram is day-to-day and could return.

At five on five, Colorado has taken 53% of the expected goals and Chicago 41%. We project 3.52 goals for COL tonight and 2.69 for CHI. Colorado's power play creates 0.70 expected goals a game to Chicago's 0.52, though the Avalanche are riding finishing well above their chances. In net, projected starters Mackenzie Blackwood (-0.44 goals saved above expected this season) and Spencer Knight (+2.94) have identical .897 save percentages, but Knight has been the better goalie by that measure and was +11.11 last season to Blackwood's +8.01.

Nathan MacKinnon is our top pick at 42% to score and 86% for a point, and as Corey Masisak of the Denver Post posted, he had "his best game of this season" in all four categories on Wednesday. Artturi Lehkonen has a nine-game point streak, though we see him due to cool. For Chicago, Connor Bedard is 34% to score. Our under-the-radar picks are Gabriel Landeskog (21% to score, 44% for a point), whose third-line shots have been dangerous, and T.J. Hughes (42% for a point), whose line creates chances.
